### Joy in Samaria
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/joy-in-samaria
Passage: Acts 8:5-8
Points:
- God used persecution to scatter believers and launch the missionary expansion of the church.
- Philip took the gospel across deep-seated cultural and ethnic barriers into Samaria.
- The Samaritan hearers were receptive partly because Jesus had previously sown seeds there.
- Philip's preaching was confirmed by signs of healing and spiritual deliverance.
- Receiving Christ brought profound communal joy to a previously burdened city.

### Day 233: Acts 8:1–13
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-233-acts-8-113.html
Passage: Acts 8:4
Points:
- Severe persecution in Jerusalem threatened to crush the early believers' public ministry.
- Efforts to silence the disciples only served to turn their message into a megaphone.
- God's providence scattered the embers of the gospel so new fires could be ignited elsewhere.
- The Lord often achieves His greatest Kingdom advances through difficult opposition rather than human comfort.
- Painful disruptions can become the very means God uses to expand our spiritual horizons.
